transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a draft sustainability-linked bond on the agenda today — five-year, fifty million dollars, targeting institutional investors. Before I sign off on this, I need to hear from each relevant function. I understand the draft currently carries a sustainability-linked label, but I want to walk through the structuring details — coupon step-up mechanics, hedge amount, and post-issuance reporting controls — to make sure we're comfortable with what we're putting in front of investors. Let's go around the table.

transcript.text: Elena, on the sustainability-linked structure specifically — I received the verified KPI methodology from our sustainability auditor this week. To retain the sustainability-linked label, the bond must include a 30-basis-point coupon step-up in the event of a missed target, and we need to commit to an annual external-assurance report for post-issuance reporting. The current draft doesn't specify either of these, so we'll need to incorporate them before this can properly go to investors as a sustainability-linked bond.

transcript.text: Elena, on the hedging and maturity side — I confirmed this morning that our refinancing schedule requires a seven-year maturity, not five. Additionally, the bank has approved swap capacity to hedge exactly 75% of a $42,000,000 issue, which comes to $31,500,000. So if we align the principal to $42,000,000 as Martin suggests, the hedge amount would be $31,500,000. We'll also need to adjust the tenor from five to seven years to match our refinancing requirements.

Neither of these controls is reflected in the current draft, and both need to be incorporated before I can sign off from a compliance standpoint.
